title: Beyond Tomorrow

evidence.note: The film was released on May 10, 1940, so its US public-domain status depends on a missing notice or a missing renewal. I did not confirm either from a primary record. I did not read the 1967-1969 Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volumes, and I did not search the Copyright Office public catalog. I can't cite a renewal-absence result. Check the renewal window by hand before treating the print as free.
evidence.source: Internet Archive, Catalog of Copyright Entries, Motion Pictures and Filmstrips 1968

evidence.note: This is a sound film. The recorded track normally shares the film's own copyright status, so the score is undetermined for the same reason as the print. I found no separate music-copyright record.
evidence.source: Internet Archive item page for the 1940 film

evidence.note: The Internet Archive page credits an original story by Mildred Cram and Adele Comandini, with a screenplay by Adele Comandini. I did not research whether the story was published separately or when, so the term of the story is unconfirmed.

The Internet Archive page says a colorized version was released in 2004 by 20th Century Fox as "Beyond Christmas". I could not confirm that from a primary source. A faithful copy of the black-and-white original adds no new US copyright. The colorization itself, and any added or new material, can carry its own protection.

editorial:
Beyond Tomorrow is a 1940 fantasy directed by A. Edward Sutherland, with an original story by Mildred Cram and Adele Comandini and a screenplay by Comandini. Three elderly industrialists die in a plane crash and return as ghosts to help reunite a young couple. Lee Garmes produced it and RKO Radio Pictures distributed it. It was released on May 10, 1940. The Christmas setting is why people look for a free copy.

It was released after the 1930 term-expiry line, so its status depends on whether the copyright was renewed. I did not confirm a renewal or a lack of one from any primary record, so every layer here is undetermined. The 1967-1969 renewal catalogs are the place to check. The film was also colorized and released as "Beyond Christmas". The Internet Archive page gives 20th Century Fox and 2004 for that release. The colorization is a separate layer and should not be assumed free.
faq: Is Beyond Tomorrow (1940) free to use?

Not confirmed. It is a 1940 film, so it is free only if its copyright was not renewed. I did not verify that from a primary record. Check the 1967-1969 renewal catalogs using the links in the dossier.
Can I use the colorized Beyond Christmas version?

Use the black-and-white print instead. The Internet Archive page says the colorized version was released in 2004 by 20th Century Fox. The colorization can be separately protected even if the original film is free.
